title: Information security policies
summary: Top-management-approved ISMS policy and supporting policies defining objectives and scope.
question: Is there a documented ISMS policy approved by top management and communicated to staff?
remediation: Create/update ISMS policy, obtain top-management approval, publish and confirm staff acknowledgement; review periodically.

title: Roles and responsibilities for information security
summary: Define governance, responsibilities, and coordination for information security.
question: Are information security roles and responsibilities defined and assigned?
remediation: Document RACI for ISMS roles, appoint owners and custodians, include responsibilities in job descriptions.

title: Coordination of security activities
summary: Ensure coordination between business units on security matters and ISMS processes.
question: Is coordination mechanism established for cross-functional security activities?
remediation: Set up security forum/steering committee and regular meetings to align security and business objectives.

title: Information security in project management
summary: Embed security requirements into project lifecycle and change initiatives.
question: Are security requirements considered in projects and major changes?
remediation: Include security criteria in project charters and change approvals; require security sign-off before go-live.

title: Inventory of information assets
summary: Maintain register of information assets and assign owners.
question: Is there an up-to-date asset inventory with assigned owners and classification?
remediation: Create asset register, keep it current, assign owners and classification labels.

title: Protection of records
summary: Protect records from loss, damage, unauthorized access and ensure retention rules.
question: Are records protected and retained according to policy and legal requirements?
remediation: Define retention schedule, protect records (access controls, backup) and document disposal procedures.

title: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
summary: Address privacy and PII protection consistent with applicable laws (e.g., GDPR/DPDP).
question: Are PII processing activities documented and privacy requirements addressed?
remediation: Map PII flows, implement privacy notices, consent records and data subject request processes.

title: Identification of legal and contractual requirements
summary: Identify applicable legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations affecting information security.
question: Does the organisation maintain a legal/regulatory register and map controls to obligations?
remediation: Maintain legal register, keep it updated and evidence compliance for audits.

title: Intellectual property rights
summary: Ensure compliance with IP rights and license management.
question: Are software licenses and intellectual property handled and tracked appropriately?
remediation: Track licenses, ensure permitted use and retain license evidence; perform periodic audits.

title: Documented operating procedures
summary: Standard operating procedures for consistent secure operations.
question: Are operating procedures documented and readily available to relevant staff?
remediation: Create runbooks, document key procedures and store in a controlled repository.

title: Change management
summary: Controlled change procedures to ensure security is considered for changes.
question: Are changes subject to formal change control with security impact assessment?
remediation: Implement change control workflow with security review and back-out plans.

title: Capacity and performance management
summary: Ensure capacity planning and performance monitoring for critical systems.
question: Is there capacity planning and monitoring to prevent performance-related failures?
remediation: Define capacity thresholds, monitor usage and plan scaling/remediation.

title: Information classification
summary: Classification scheme for information sensitivity and handling requirements.
question: Are classification labels and handling rules defined and applied?
remediation: Define taxonomy, apply labels in systems and train staff on handling rules.

title: Media handling and disposal
summary: Secure handling and disposal of storage media.
question: Are media handling, transport and secure disposal procedures defined and enforced?
remediation: Implement media handling procedures, wipe or destroy media per policy and document disposal.

title: Asset handling while off-premises
summary: Protect information assets used outside organisational premises.
question: Are remote/off-premises asset protections defined (laptops, removable media)?
remediation: Encrypt devices, require VPN/endpoint controls and maintain asset logs for off-premises equipment.

title: Supplier security
summary: Security requirements for suppliers and third-party relationships.
question: Are supplier security requirements defined and assessed during onboarding?
remediation: Include security clauses in contracts, perform supplier due diligence and periodic reviews.

title: Access control policy
summary: Define and enforce access control policies following least privilege principles.
question: Is access control policy documented and enforced across systems?
remediation: Implement RBAC or equivalent model, approval workflows for provisioning and periodic reviews.

title: User access management
summary: Provisioning, review, and revocation processes for user accounts.
question: Are user accounts reviewed, and deprovisioning performed promptly on role change/leaver?
remediation: Automate deprovisioning, schedule access reviews and keep provisioning logs.

title: Privileged access management
summary: Control, monitor and limit privileged accounts and activities.
question: Are privileged accounts controlled with strict approvals and monitoring (MFA, logging)?
remediation: Enforce MFA, use PAM where needed, and log and review privileged activity.

title: Secure authentication
summary: Authentication mechanisms and policies (passwords, MFA, session controls).
question: Are authentication mechanisms (password policies, MFA) implemented for critical access?
remediation: Set password complexity, enforce MFA for sensitive roles and monitor authentication anomalies.

title: Information access restriction
summary: Restrict access to data and resources based on business need-to-know.
question: Is data access restricted per classification and business need?
remediation: Design least-privilege access models and enforce via ACLs or RBAC.

title: Logging and monitoring
summary: Collect and retain logs centrally for detection and investigation.
question: Are critical systems centrally logged and monitored with alerts and retention policy?
remediation: Deploy centralised logging/SIEM, configure alerts and retain logs per retention policy.

title: Event detection and response
summary: Processes to detect, report and respond to security incidents.
question: Is there an incident detection and response process and an incident register?
remediation: Implement IR plan, define playbooks, test via tabletop exercises and maintain incident log.

title: Information security incident management
summary: Manage incidents lifecycle and lessons learned.
question: Are incidents recorded, investigated and lessons incorporated into controls?
remediation: Record incidents, conduct root-cause analysis and update controls and training accordingly.

title: Business continuity management
summary: Protect business processes and ensure recovery for critical services.
question: Are BCP and DR plans documented and validated by tests?
remediation: Perform BIA, document BCP/DR procedures, and test recovery plans periodically.

title: Backup
summary: Ensure reliable backups and restore testing for data and systems.
question: Are backups scheduled, stored securely, and periodically tested for restoration?
remediation: Implement encrypted backups, periodic restore tests and retention policies.

title: Learning from security incidents
summary: Use incidents to improve controls, processes and staff awareness.
question: Does the organisation capture lessons from incidents and implement improvements?
remediation: Run post-incident reviews, document lessons and apply control improvements and training.

title: Collection and preservation of evidence
summary: Preserve evidence for investigations and legal requirements.
question: Are procedures in place to collect and preserve forensic evidence securely?
remediation: Define evidentiary procedures, secure chain-of-custody and preserve logs for investigations.

title: ICT readiness for business continuity
summary: Ensure ICT resilience supports business continuity during disruptions.
question: Are ICT continuity measures (redundancy, failover) implemented for critical systems?
remediation: Design redundancy, failover strategies and test them during BCP exercises.

title: Identification of legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
summary: Track laws and contractual obligations relevant to information security.
question: Is there a legal/regulatory register and mapping to ISMS controls?
remediation: Maintain and review legal register and map obligations to ISMS controls; keep supporting evidence.

title: Protection of records
summary: Retention and protection of records supporting ISMS activities.
question: Are records retained and protected per policy and legal requirements?
remediation: Define retention, protect records from tampering and ensure secure disposal.

title: Independent review of information security
summary: Periodic independent reviews or audits of the ISMS.
question: Are independent reviews or internal audits conducted and findings remediated?
remediation: Schedule audits, track findings to closure and report to management.

title: Compliance with policies and standards
summary: Ensure staff comply with security policies and standards.
question: Is compliance with ISMS policies monitored and enforced?
remediation: Perform policy compliance checks, disciplinary measures for violations and record evidence.

title: Documented operating procedures
summary: Consistent, secure procedures for key operations and tasks.
question: Are operational procedures documented, versioned and accessible?
remediation: Store SOPs in a controlled repository, control versions and ensure staff awareness.

title: Protection of PII and privacy
summary: Additional controls to protect personal data beyond general ISMS controls.
question: Are privacy principles (minimization, purpose limitation) implemented where PII is processed?
remediation: Perform PIA/DPIA, implement minimization, consent management, and DSAR processes.

title: Documentation and operating procedures for security
summary: Maintain documented procedures to support secure operations and compliance.
question: Are documentation practices defined for security processes and evidence maintained?
remediation: Standardise documentation templates and store evidence tied to control implementation.

title: Screening
summary: Background checks for employees and contractors where relevant to their roles.
question: Are pre-employment screening and background checks performed according to risk?
remediation: Define screening requirements by role and record screening outcomes.

title: Terms and conditions of employment
summary: Include security responsibilities in employment terms and contracts.
question: Do contracts include confidentiality and security obligations?
remediation: Update employment contracts with confidentiality/security clauses and obtain signed acknowledgements.

title: Information security awareness, education and training
summary: Provide security awareness and role-based training to staff.
question: Is a formal security awareness and role-specific training program in place?
remediation: Deliver regular awareness, role-based training and measure participation and effectiveness.

title: Disciplinary process
summary: Enforce disciplinary measures for security policy violations.
question: Are disciplinary processes defined for breaches of security policy?
remediation: Document disciplinary procedures and apply them consistently when violations occur.

title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
summary: Ensure access removal and obligations continue post-termination or role change.
question: Are exit and role-change procedures defined to revoke access and assets?
remediation: Implement checklists for exit, revoke access promptly and recover assets.

title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
summary: Use NDAs to protect confidential information where needed.
question: Are NDAs or confidentiality agreements used with staff and third parties handling sensitive data?
remediation: Issue NDAs where applicable and retain signed copies as evidence.

title: Remote working
summary: Controls for secure remote work (VPN, device security, policies).
question: Are remote working policies and technical controls (VPN, EDR) implemented?
remediation: Define remote work policy, enforce device security and monitor remote access.

title: Physical security perimeter
summary: Physical protections for sensitive areas and equipment.
question: Are physical access controls and environmental protections in place for critical areas?
remediation: Use access controls, CCTV, environmental monitoring and visitor logs for sensitive areas.

title: Physical entry controls
summary: Control physical access to premises and areas housing critical systems.
question: Are physical entry controls (badges, locks) enforced and monitored?
remediation: Implement badge systems, visitor procedures and regular reviews of access lists.

title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
summary: Ensure secure layout and protection for facilities and offices.
question: Are workspaces and facilities protected against unauthorized access and hazards?
remediation: Apply physical separation, secure storage and access zoning for sensitive facilities.

title: Physical security monitoring
summary: Monitor physical spaces for security events and anomalies.
question: Is physical security monitored (CCTV, alarms) with retained logs?
remediation: Install monitoring devices, retain footage per retention policy and review alerts.

title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
summary: Mitigate threats from environmental hazards, fire, water and similar risks.
question: Are environmental protections (fire suppression, climate control) applied to critical locations?
remediation: Install fire detection, suppression, and environmental controls with testing schedules.

title: Working in secure areas
summary: Controls for working within secure zones or classified areas.
question: Are procedures defined for working in secure areas (authorization, supervision)?
remediation: Define secure-area procedures, limit access and require supervision for visitors and contractors.

title: Clear desk and clear screen
summary: Enforce clear desk and screen practices to reduce data exposure risk.
question: Is a clear desk/screen policy enforced to protect sensitive information?
remediation: Formalize policy, run awareness and spot checks to enforce compliance.

title: Equipment siting and protection
summary: Place and protect equipment to mitigate environmental and security risks.
question: Is equipment sited and protected to prevent tampering or environmental damage?
remediation: Define siting guidance, enforce protection and undertake periodic checks.

title: Security of assets off-premises
summary: Protect assets used or stored outside company premises.
question: Are controls in place to protect equipment and information used off-premises?
remediation: Encrypt off-premises devices, require secure transport and report loss/theft promptly.

title: Storage media protection
summary: Protect storage media from unauthorized access and damage.
question: Are storage media protected in transit and storage with proper labeling and handling?
remediation: Label media, encrypt/secure storage and define transport procedures.

title: Supporting utilities
summary: Protect utilities (power, water, HVAC) that support information processing facilities.
question: Are critical utilities protected and monitored to ensure continuity?
remediation: Redundancy for critical utilities, monitoring and maintenance contracts in place.

title: Cabling security
summary: Protect cabling infrastructure from interception and damage.
question: Are cabling and network routes physically protected and documented?
remediation: Use protected cabling channels, label cables and limit access to telecom rooms.

title: Equipment maintenance
summary: Maintain equipment per vendor guidance to ensure reliability and security.
question: Are maintenance schedules and secure maintenance procedures in place?
remediation: Document maintenance, use authorised vendors and track maintenance records.

title: Secure disposal or reuse of equipment
summary: Ensure secure disposal or sanitization of equipment before reuse or disposal.
question: Are procedures in place to wipe or destroy data before disposal or reuse?
remediation: Define sanitization methods, maintain disposal logs and ensure responsible disposal vendors.

title: User endpoint devices
summary: Manage and secure user endpoint devices (laptops, mobiles).
question: Are endpoint security controls (EDR, configuration baselines) enforced for user devices?
remediation: Deploy endpoint protection, enforce baselines and perform periodic audits of device posture.

title: Privileged access rights
summary: Manage and control privileged user access and activities.
question: Are privileged accounts restricted, documented and monitored?
remediation: Implement PAM, restrict privileged use and review privileged accounts regularly.

title: Information access restriction
summary: Restrict access to information and processing facilities.
question: Is access to systems and information restricted based on business need and classification?
remediation: Define access rules per classification and implement technical enforcement (ACLs/RBAC).

title: Access to source code
summary: Protect source code and manage access and change processes.
question: Is source code access controlled and secure build/review processes used?
remediation: Limit source code access, use code review and secure repositories with audit logs.

title: Secure authentication
summary: Strong authentication mechanisms for systems and applications.
question: Is multi-factor authentication or equivalent controls applied where required?
remediation: Enforce MFA for remote/privileged access and document authentication policies.

title: Capacity management
summary: Manage resource capacity to avoid degradation and outages.
question: Is capacity planning performed for critical systems with monitoring in place?
remediation: Implement monitoring, alerts and capacity planning processes.

title: Protection against malware
summary: Controls to prevent, detect and recover from malware infections.
question: Are anti-malware controls and updating processes in place?
remediation: Deploy AV/EDR, schedule signature/definition updates and scan regularly.

title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
summary: Identify, assess and remediate technical vulnerabilities timely.
question: Is vulnerability management (scanning, patching) performed and tracked?
remediation: Run regular scans, maintain patching SLAs and track remediation until closure.

title: Configuration management
summary: Secure and consistent configuration of systems and network devices.
question: Are secure configuration baselines and change control enforced for systems?
remediation: Define hardening guides, apply baselines and monitor deviation.

title: Information deletion
summary: Ensure secure deletion of information in systems and media when no longer required.
question: Are secure deletion and retention rules implemented for data lifecycles?
remediation: Implement secure deletion tools, retention schedules and evidence of deletion.

title: Data masking
summary: Mask sensitive data in non-production or where full data exposure is unnecessary.
question: Is sensitive data masked/anonymized in test and non-production environments?
remediation: Implement masking/obfuscation for test data and restrict access to production data.

title: Data leakage prevention
summary: Prevent unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive data from systems.
question: Are DLP controls or equivalent measures in place to detect/prevent data exfiltration?
remediation: Deploy DLP policies, monitor channels and block unauthorized transfers.

title: Information backup
summary: Regular backups and tested restores for resilience.
question: Are backups performed, secured and periodically tested for integrity and restore?
remediation: Define RPO/RTO, encrypt backups and test restores on a schedule.

title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
summary: Redundancy for critical processing facilities to ensure availability.
question: Are critical systems hosted with redundancy or failover provisions?
remediation: Design redundant architectures and test failover and recovery procedures.

title: Logging
summary: Capture relevant logs for security monitoring and investigations.
question: Are logs configured appropriately and collected centrally for critical systems?
remediation: Centralise logging, define retention and monitor for key events/alerts.

title: Monitoring activities
summary: Monitor systems and networks for security events and anomalies.
question: Is continuous or scheduled monitoring configured with alerting on suspicious events?
remediation: Tune alerts, implement SIEM and ensure staffed monitoring or escalation.

title: Clock synchronisation
summary: Synchronize clocks across systems to ensure log coherence and forensic reliability.
question: Are system clocks synchronized to a trusted time source for log integrity?
remediation: Configure NTP/time servers and verify across systems for forensic consistency.

title: Use of privileged utility programs
summary: Control use of utilities that can override system controls and access data.
question: Are privileged utilities restricted and usage monitored?
remediation: Restrict utility use to authorised personnel and audit utility usage regularly.

title: Installation of software on operational systems
summary: Control installation of software to prevent malware and unauthorized applications.
question: Is software installation on production systems restricted and approved?
remediation: Enforce change control and run whitelisting or authorised-install mechanisms.

title: Network controls
summary: Design and enforce network security controls (segmentation, firewalls).
question: Are network segmentation, firewalls and secure configurations implemented?
remediation: Implement network zones, firewall rules and monitoring of cross-zone traffic.

title: Security of network services
summary: Secure provision and consumption of external and internal network services.
question: Are network services evaluated and secured before deployment?
remediation: Assess service security, enforce secure service configurations and monitor performance.

title: Segregation in networks
summary: Separate networks by function and risk to limit exposures.
question: Is segregation implemented for user, server and management networks?
remediation: Design VLANs/segments, enforce routing restrictions and review segmentation effectiveness.

title: Web filtering
summary: Control and filter web traffic to reduce exposure to malicious content.
question: Are web filtering or proxy controls used to limit risky web access?
remediation: Deploy filtering solutions and define acceptable-use rules for web access.

title: Use of cryptography
summary: Appropriate use of cryptography to protect confidentiality and integrity.
question: Is cryptography applied where needed and key management defined?
remediation: Define cryptographic policy, manage keys securely and document algorithm choices.

title: Secure development lifecycle
summary: Integrate security into SDLC including requirements, design and testing.
question: Is security integrated into development lifecycle with SAST/DAST and code review?
remediation: Adopt secure SDLC practices, include security gates and test for vulnerabilities pre-release.

title: Application security requirements
summary: Define security requirements for applications and services.
question: Are application security requirements captured and validated during development?
remediation: Document requirements, enforce secure coding and include security tests in CI/CD.

title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
summary: Design systems with security principles and threat modelling.
question: Are architecture reviews and threat modelling performed for critical systems?
remediation: Conduct architecture reviews and threat-modelling sessions and document decisions.

title: Security testing in development and acceptance
summary: Test for security issues before release and on major changes.
question: Are security tests performed during development and acceptance phases?
remediation: Include SAST/DAST in CI, run penetration tests and include security acceptance criteria.

title: Outsourced development
summary: Manage security when development is outsourced to third parties.
question: Are outsourcing agreements for development including security clauses and oversight?
remediation: Include security requirements in contracts and perform supplier audits for outsourced development.

title: Separation of development, test and production environments
summary: Keep dev/test and prod environments separate to prevent data leaks and unintended changes.
question: Are dev/test environments segregated from production and protected?
remediation: Enforce environment separation, mask production data in test and restrict access to production.

title: Change management
summary: Formal change management process for system changes to maintain stability and security.
question: Is a formal change management process applied for system and application changes?
remediation: Implement change control workflow with approvals, testing and rollback plans.

title: Test information
summary: Protect test data and environments to avoid exposure of sensitive information.
question: Is test information (data) protected and sanitized before use in non-prod environments?
remediation: Mask or generate synthetic data for test environments and control access to test systems.

title: Change control
summary: Ensure changes are reviewed for security impact and properly authorised.
question: Are changes assessed for security impact and approved by relevant parties?
remediation: Include security reviewers in change approvals and retain change evidence.

title: Supplier relationships
summary: Manage supplier security lifecycle from selection to termination.
question: Are supplier selection, due diligence and monitoring processes defined for suppliers?
remediation: Perform supplier risk assessments, include SLAs/security clauses and monitor supplier performance.

title: Supplier service delivery
summary: Ensure suppliers meet security and service delivery expectations.
question: Are supplier service levels and security obligations measured and enforced?
remediation: Track SLA/security KPIs and remediate supplier issues per contract terms.

title: Supplier monitoring
summary: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of supplier security posture.
question: Is there a program to continuously monitor and review critical suppliers?
remediation: Schedule periodic reviews, audits and escalate supplier non-compliance.

title: Information transfer policies and procedures
summary: Securely transfer information with controls for confidentiality and integrity.
question: Are secure methods and policies used for transfers (encryption, secure channels)?
remediation: Define transfer policies, use encrypted channels and document transfer approvals.

title: Agreements on information transfers
summary: Agreements that document terms for secure information exchange with third parties.
question: Are inter-organization transfer agreements defining security responsibilities in place?
remediation: Draft and sign agreements specifying security measures and responsibilities for transfers.

title: Monitoring and review of supplier services
summary: Regularly review supplier deliverables for security compliance.
question: Are supplier deliverables reviewed for security and compliance with contractual terms?
remediation: Implement supplier performance reviews and evidence collection for audits.

title: Management of third-party security risks
summary: Assess and manage security risks introduced by third-party services/providers.
question: Are third-party risks identified, assessed and mitigated?
remediation: Maintain third-party risk register and implement mitigation plans for critical vendors.

title: Information security incident management
summary: Comprehensive incident management processes including detection, reporting and response.
question: Is there a defined incident management lifecycle including reporting and post-incident actions?
remediation: Document IR plan, assign roles, test playbooks and record remediation and lessons learned.

title: Learning from incidents
summary: Capture lessons from incidents and strengthen controls accordingly.
question: Are incident lessons captured and used to improve controls and training?
remediation: Perform RCA, update controls and include findings in awareness programs.

title: Collection of evidence
summary: Procedures to gather and preserve evidence during incidents and investigations.
question: Are forensic evidence collection and chain-of-custody processes documented?
remediation: Define forensic procedures and preserve evidence with secure storage and access controls.

title: Business continuity and information security
summary: Integrate information security into BCP and DR planning.
question: Is information security integrated into BCP/DR plans with clear recovery priorities?
remediation: Conduct BIA, integrate IS controls in BCP and test DR plans regularly.

title: Availability of information processing facilities
summary: Ensure availability and resilience of information processing assets.
question: Are measures in place to maintain availability of critical processing facilities?
remediation: Implement redundancy, failover and capacity planning to reduce downtime risk.

title: Legal and contractual requirements
summary: Identify and comply with legal, regulatory and contractual obligations related to information security.
question: Is there a mechanism to track and evidence compliance with legal and contractual obligations?
remediation: Maintain obligations register, map to controls and collect evidence for audits.

title: Protection of organisational records
summary: Protect records that are important for business continuity and legal compliance.
question: Are organisational records protected and retrievable when needed?
remediation: Implement access controls, retention and backup strategies for critical records.

title: Requirements for information systems
summary: Define security requirements for information systems to meet business needs.
question: Are security requirements documented for major information systems and services?
remediation: Capture security requirements, include them in procurement and development processes.

title: Security in supplier relationships
summary: Ensure suppliers meet security requirements across their lifecycle.
question: Are supplier security requirements included in contracts and reviewed periodically?
remediation: Include security KPIs in contracts and conduct supplier assessments and audits.

title: System acquisition, development and maintenance
summary: Security requirements must be applied to acquired or developed systems.
question: Are security requirements considered in acquisitions and system development lifecycles?
remediation: Include security acceptance in procurement and development checklists and review vendor security.

title: Change management for organisational systems
summary: Manage changes to organizational systems to mitigate security impacts.
question: Is there a change management process to asses and approve system changes?
remediation: Establish change advisory board, require security assessment and maintain change logs.

title: Secure development policy
summary: Policies that enforce secure development practices and responsibilities.
question: Is a secure development policy documented and enforced for software projects?
remediation: Create secure development policy, include security training and governance in SDLC.

title: Protection of test data
summary: Control and protect test data to avoid exposure of production personal data.
question: Is production data masked or prevented from use in test environments?
remediation: Implement masking or synthetic data and enforce access controls for test systems.

title: Security in network services
summary: Ensure network services are designed and configured securely.
question: Are network services evaluated and hardened according to security requirements?
remediation: Harden network services and document configurations; review changes.

title: Protection of system documentation
summary: Control access to system documentation to prevent misuse.
question: Is system documentation protected and access limited to authorised personnel?
remediation: Secure documentation repositories and apply access controls and versioning.

title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
summary: Identify and remediate vulnerabilities in systems and applications.
question: Is there a formal vulnerability management program with timelines for remediation?
remediation: Schedule scans, prioritise vulnerabilities and track remediation until closure.

title: Information deletion and retention
summary: Manage retention and secure deletion in line with legal requirements.
question: Are retention schedules defined and secure deletion applied when data is no longer required?
remediation: Define retention policies and implement secure deletion with verification where necessary.

title: Protection against malware
summary: Measures to prevent and respond to malware infections across systems.
question: Are malware protections in place and are response plans defined?
remediation: Deploy AV/EDR, update definitions and include malware in incident playbooks.

title: Monitoring of system use
summary: Monitor systems for misuse and security-relevant activity.
question: Is system usage monitored for anomalies and misuse with alerting mechanisms?
remediation: Implement monitoring rules, tune alerts and ensure review processes for incidents.

title: Network security management
summary: Manage and protect network infrastructure and services to prevent threats.
question: Are firewalls, segmentation and secure network designs applied to protect critical systems?
remediation: Design layered network controls and monitor network traffic for suspicious patterns.

title: Segregation of networks
summary: Separate networks to limit blast radius and enforce access boundaries.
question: Are networks segregated by function and data sensitivity?
remediation: Implement segregation (VLANs/Zones) and control inter-segment traffic with ACLs.

title: Security of network services
summary: Ensure network services consumed or offered are secure and monitored.
question: Are external and internal network services validated for security before use?
remediation: Perform security assessments and enforce secure configuration for services.

title: System acquisition, development and maintenance
summary: Ensure secure practices across system procurement and lifecycle.
question: Are security requirements considered during procurement and system lifecycle management?
remediation: Include security clauses in procurement, enforce secure lifecycle practices and vendor checks.

title: Test and acceptance
summary: Security testing and acceptance prior to deployment to production.
question: Is security testing performed and accepted before system deployment?
remediation: Require security test sign-offs and include remediation of findings before release.

title: Change control for software and systems
summary: Controlled software changes to minimise security impact and maintain traceability.
question: Are software changes controlled with security impact assessment and rollback plans?
remediation: Use version control, CI/CD gates and documented rollback procedures for releases.

title: Secure build and deployment
summary: Secure build pipelines and hardened deployment processes.
question: Are build/deploy pipelines secured and artefacts verified prior to deployment?
remediation: Harden CI/CD, sign artefacts and restrict pipeline access to authorised users.

title: Protection of development environments
summary: Protect development, test and integration environments from unauthorized access and data leaks.
question: Are development and test environments protected and isolated from production?
remediation: Isolate environments, mask data and control access to non-prod resources.

title: Outsourced development and maintenance
summary: Manage security when development and maintenance are performed by third parties.
question: Are outsourced development activities contracted with clear security responsibilities?
remediation: Include security SLAs in contracts and audit outsourced processes periodically.

title: Information transfer policies
summary: Policies and protections for information exchange across boundaries.
question: Are secure information transfer policies and tools used for data exchange?
remediation: Define and enforce transfer policies, use encryption and logging for transfers.

title: Electronic messaging controls
summary: Secure use of email and messaging channels to prevent leakage and impersonation.
question: Are secure email/messaging controls (SPF/DKIM, DLP) in place?
remediation: Implement email authentication, DLP for sensitive content and user training against phishing.

title: Information classification and handling for transfer
summary: Ensure classification and handling rules are applied during transfers.
question: Is classification respected during transfers and are handling rules enforced?
remediation: Tag data during transfer and enforce handling via automated controls or DLP.

title: Supplier relationships and information sharing
summary: Securely manage information sharing with suppliers and partners.
question: Are information sharing agreements and controls documented with third parties?
remediation: Create sharing agreements, limit shared data and record sharing events for audits.

title: Information security incident reporting and communication
summary: Timely internal and external reporting and communication about incidents.
question: Are incident reporting lines, external notifications and communication plans defined?
remediation: Define incident reporting channels, notification templates and communication plans for stakeholders.

title: Incident response planning and testing
summary: Maintain and exercise incident response plans and playbooks.
question: Are incident response plans documented and tested by exercises and simulations?
remediation: Develop playbooks, run tabletop exercises and update plans based on test outcomes.

title: Collection and preservation of evidence
summary: Securely collect evidence during incidents for investigation and legal processes.
question: Are forensic evidence collection procedures available and enacted when required?
remediation: Document forensic procedures and maintain chain-of-custody for collected evidence.

title: Lessons learned and improvement
summary: Feed incident findings into continuous improvement of ISMS and controls.
question: Are incident learnings documented and used to improve controls and training?
